title: Hanoverian envoys Diede and Reck at Regensburg, 1730 (NLA Hannover, Hann. 9g Nr. 1687 and Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1): key of the type A letter cipher rebuilt from the chancery's plaintext of the time and validated on an unglossed page

documents.shelfmark: Hannover, Niedersächsisches Landesarchiv, Hann. 9g Nr. 1687 (chiffrierte Berichte aus Regensburg, 1730), aufn 004, 025-036, 056-057, 060-068
documents.route: Wilhelm von Diede (zum Fürstenstein) and Reck, Hanoverian envoys at the Imperial Diet -> George II / the Geheimer Rat in Hannover

documents.shelfmark: Hannover, Niedersächsisches Landesarchiv, Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1 (Einzelne Relationen aus Regensburg 1730-1731), aufn 0004
documents.route: Diede and Reck (Regensburg) -> George II (London copy, Deutsche Kanzlei)

plaintext.source: No gloss on aufn 0004; the start of the same postscript (aufn 0003, 5 cipher lines) carries a full interlinear decipherment of the time.

transcription.notes: 242 groups, transcribed by one agent without the key and frozen before decoding; the first 160 are the held-out portion of measurement 2.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of German letters: dotted groups of 2-4 digits (5-1497), about one group per letter, 3-6 homophones for frequent letters, written in lines inside clear relations; a few word or syllable codes (Chur Mayntz 216.123.53, Chur Cölln 270.333; 841 = ich probably). 166 values in the rebuilt table.

prior_solution.where: In the archive: the clear text of the P.S. ad Relat. 16 of the time (Nr. 1687 aufn 065R-068L) and partial interlinear decipherments in Nr. 1687 and Nr. 1149/1 (aufn 0003, 0006-0008, 0102-0103). No key sheet found in either file. Lead 1659 vetting (2 Nov 2026): nothing on DECODE, Cryptiana or Lasry's lists; no edition. targets/mecklenburg1734 is another system. No target, branch or PR for Nr. 1687 or Nr. 1149/1 in this repository (main 6a94e2f0e, 11 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's Archivportal-D sweep found Nr. 1687 (lead 1659). Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocols, key and held-out portions hashed before viewing; one measurement each; one re-test of an unchanged key) and approved publication. AI agents surveyed, transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Nr. 1687: cipher runs of aufn 004, 025-036, 056-057, 060-065 (3,636 groups) and the clear P.S. ad Relat. 16 (065R-068L).
Alignment of glosses line by line, then a nomenclator-with-nulls model: no stable key (the glosses run on as continuous text under the line).

Relat. 16 cipher (060-065) aligned letter by letter with its clear P.S. of the time: about one group per letter, homophonic letter substitution; key frozen by SHA-256 (83 sure, 66 probable, 17 doubtful).

Measurement 1 (pre-registered), Nr. 1687 aufn 033-036, 160 glossed groups: one Smith-Waterman alignment, 0.244 vs 0.050 for the best of 200 shuffled keys; thresholds >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30 not met. Post hoc, run by run, no verdict value: 0.738 vs 0.412.

Measurement 2 (pre-registered single re-test of the unchanged key), Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1 aufn 0004, 160 unglossed groups: dictionary coverage M5 0.656 vs 0.325 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (mean 0.196), margin 0.331; thresholds >= 0.60 and margin >= 0.30, calibrated and hashed beforehand.
Aufn 0004, groups 1-160 read as German: sure 106, probable 39, restored 12, unresolved 3; agrees with the gloss of the time on aufn 0003. Groups 161-242 decoded as unmeasured exploration.

Survey of all 605 images of Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1: type A cipher in three pieces of Jan-Feb 1730 (about 975 groups, about 685 glossed), a type B 4-digit system in a piece of 3 Aug 1730 (about 900 groups, pale gloss), not attacked.

Integration check (Daniel's session): frozen/1149-1/scripts/m5.py re-run on frozen/1687/KEY.tsv (SHA-256 4d83b4f7... matches KEY.sha256) and H-0004.codes: coverage 0.656, controls mean 0.196, best 0.325, margin 0.331, as reported.

Integration: the frozen key applied to all transcribed type A runs of Nr. 1687 (decode1687.py -> decryption-1687.txt): 3,630 groups parsed, 3,426 with a sure/probable value (contributor: 3,431 of 3,636). Spot check aufn 056 R7-R16 (unglossed) reads 'nechst tagen einen der ministrorum nach mainz absenden umb daselbst unter andern in der mecklenburgischen sache'. No word-by-word reading made.
Integration: tried to fetch Nr. 1687 aufn 158 from Arcinsys to transcribe Relat. 25; the host is refused by this session's network policy, as is Wikimedia Commons (portraits).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the clear P.S. ad Relat. 16 written at the time (Nr. 1687 aufn 065R-068L) aligned with the cipher of Relat. 16, and validated once on an unglossed page of the London copies (Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1 aufn 0004) after a first, failed measurement on Nr. 1687.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py). Measurement 1 (Nr. 1687 aufn 033-036, one Smith-Waterman character alignment against the gloss) FAILED: 0.244 vs 0.050, thresholds >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30; post hoc run by run 0.738 vs 0.412, no verdict value. Measurement 2, the single re-test of the unchanged key (Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1 aufn 0004, 160 unglossed groups, transcribed without the key and hashed): M5 dictionary coverage 0.656 vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.325 (mean 0.196), margin 0.331; thresholds >= 0.60 and margin >= 0.30 calibrated on Nr. 1687 and hashed in advance -> pass. M5 measures dictionary coverage, not character agreement with a plaintext (there is none for aufn 0004).

texts.label: Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1 aufn 0004, P.S. ad Relat. 1 (2 Jan 1730): groups 1-160, the held-out portion
texts.summary: Continuing the postscript of aufn 0003: someone's good and confidential friendship, in the Electoral College as well as in the Corpus Evangelicorum, is of no small importance, now above all, and daily gives occasion...
texts.note: Decode with the frozen key; 106 sure, 39 probable, 12 restored (outside the key, from context, after the measurement), 3 unresolved of 160 groups. Agrees word for word with the gloss of the time on aufn 0003 (not used). Groups 161-242 of the page are unmeasured exploration, not part of this text.

reading_review.note: decode read as German sentences, one passage that starts and ends mid-sentence; 145 of 160 groups read by the key, 12 restored from context, 3 unresolved (key value conflicts); agrees with the 0003 gloss; one reader

texts.label: Hann. 9g Nr. 1687, transcribed type A runs (aufn 004, 025-036, 056-057, 060-065): raw decode with the frozen key
texts.summary: Diede and Reck's ciphered passages in their Regensburg relations of January-March 1730 to Hannover, on the Imperial Diet and the Mecklenburg affair; Relat. 16 has the chancery's clear P.S. of the time, from which the key was learned.
texts.note: Mechanical decode, one line per cipher line, '?' = outside the key; spot checks only (aufn 027, 033-036, 056). Not counted as a reading.

outcome.notes: Lead 1659 (Hann. 9g Nr. 1687, 1691) was closed as a duplicate of catalogue 598 without a cipher page opened; Nr. 1687 is dated 1730 and uses a dotted letter cipher, not the code of targets/mecklenburg1734. The chancery's own plaintext of 1730 covers much of the material, so we claim the key and its validation, not a solution. Hann. 92 Nr. 1149/1 is a new source for leads 1658/1659.
